page: Amazon Web Services c5ad.24xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the Nitro hypervisor and powered by an AMD EPYC 7R32 processor running at 3.3 GHz. The instance delivers 96 virtual CPUs across 48 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. It includes 192 GB of DDR4 memory clocked at 3 GHz, providing a standard compute-optimized memory ratio of 2 GB per vCPU. The hardware setup also integrates 3,800 GB of fast local NVMe SSD storage and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 20 Gbps. It lacks hardware acceleration like GPUs and does not support AVX-512 or AMX vector extensions, relying on standard AVX, SHA-NI, and AES instruction sets.

Benchmark results show notable strengths in parallel integer throughput, cryptographic routines, and high-frequency memory access. The instance achieved top-tier performance in PassMark CPU encryption tests and placed in the top 25 percent for overall PassMark CPU score, extended instructions, software compilation with Clang, and ray tracing. Memory throughput is solid, highlighted by strong L1/L2 cache read bandwidth and strong key-value performance, handling over 80 million Redis SET operations per second. However, single-threaded processing reflects lower per-core throughput, as seen in stress-ng single-core tests ranking in the lowest 10 percent.

From an infrastructure perspective, pairing 96 dedicated vCPUs with 3,800 GB of directly attached NVMe storage delivers high operational efficiency for workloads that require immediate local scratch capacity alongside heavy parallel computing. The local NVMe drives eliminate network-attached storage latency for transient files, though the ephemeral nature of instance stores requires architecture designs that tolerate data volatility upon instance termination.

The c5ad.24xlarge is best suited for parallel processing workloads, multi-threaded continuous integration and build pipelines, batch data processing, distributed caching tiers, and high-concurrency database operations needing rapid local disk I/O without incurring external storage overhead.
description: Amazon Web Services c5ad.24xlarge is a compute-optimized instance featuring 96 vCPUs (48 physical cores) powered by a 3.3 GHz AMD EPYC 7R32 processor on the Nitro system. Configured with a 1:2 compute-to-memory ratio, it supplies 192 GB of DDR4 RAM alongside 3,800 GB of direct-attached NVMe SSD storage and 20 Gbps baseline networking. Synthetic benchmarks indicate strong parallel capabilities, particularly in cryptographic operations, multi-threaded Clang compilation, ray tracing, and in-memory key-value workloads executing over 80 million Redis SET operations per second. While single-thread execution speed is modest and AVX-512 extensions are absent, the dense core allocation and fast local storage make this instance cost-effective for high-throughput batch workloads, CI/CD build farms, and parallel database tasks requiring rapid local scratch capacity.
